criterion: behaviour-preservation: changed rule with a second reader
finding: Fix selects any `still small` row but never says the latest row across both grill sections wins, so a later `too big` row does not stop the fix.
why: The latest-row-wins rule lives only in GRILL-LOG-FORMAT.md and D-14; fix would apply a superseded call.
fix: State in step 2 that the row with the latest time across both grill sections decides; a latest `too big` row stops.
evidence: fix:35 "with a `still small` size-call row for its Work id in the `GRILL-LOG.md` beside it" vs GRILL-LOG-FORMAT.md:110 "across both grill sections, the row with the latest time wins"

criterion: behaviour-preservation: reworked control flow in an existing procedure
finding: A re-run in a handed worktree gets contradictory instructions: step 2 makes the handed branch and its tip the Diagnosis branch and Base, while step 5 keeps the recorded Base and Diagnosis branch from an existing DIAGNOSIS.md.
why: Both rules fire on a second in-place call for the same bug.
fix: In step 5, say a handed worktree's branch and tip replace the recorded Base and Diagnosis branch.
evidence: diagnose:33 "its branch is the Diagnosis branch and its tip commit the Base" vs :36 "keep its Work id, Ticket key, Base, Diagnosis branch and Outside writes"

criterion: behaviour-preservation: dropped step / path input location
finding: With a DIAGNOSIS.md path input no worktree was handed over, so 'the worktree fix handed over' has no referent and fix falls to the Diagnosis-branch worktree (a second worktree); the delta also dropped 'git checkout <Diagnosis branch> -- <test path>', so a caller's worktree lacks the failing test.
why: A path input from a caller in its own linked worktree recreates the second-worktree problem D-14 removed, and the failing test cannot be watched failing.
fix: Fix in the linked worktree fix runs in (outside one, the Diagnosis-branch worktree) and bring the failing test in from the Diagnosis branch when it is not there.
evidence: fix:39 "in the diagnosis worktree: the worktree fix handed over, else the one on the Diagnosis branch"; removed: "Bring in the diagnosis's failing test first (`git checkout <Diagnosis branch> -- <test path>` when it is not there)"

finding: Delta edits WORKFLOW-FEEDBACK.md, which is not in contract 0004 ## Scope; D-16 records it but supersedes no Scope passage.
why: A decision entry waives only the spec passage it quotes (D-16 'Supersedes: none').
fix: Record a decision superseding the Scope list for this file, or revert the edit.
evidence: D-16: 'one line outside Scope'; Supersedes: none

criterion: caller whose contract the diff changed but did not update
finding: A handed-over worktree makes the invoker's own branch the Diagnosis branch with only its tip commit as Base: no Base branch is named (DIAGNOSIS-FORMAT requires the branch and its commit id), the SDD §4 rows for the diagnosis branch and worktree no longer hold, and fix's 'gone -> create-worktree --branch <Diagnosis branch>' could target an invoker branch.
why: The consumed format and SDD §4 disagree with the skill about the handed case.
fix: Name the Base branch for a handed worktree, record a decision narrowing SDD §4 for that case, and keep fix from cutting onto an invoker branch.
evidence: diagnose:33 'its branch is the Diagnosis branch and its tip commit the Base'; DIAGNOSIS-FORMAT.md:16 'Base | the branch the reproduction started from, and its commit id'; SDD §4 'Diagnosis branch | ... pushed only by `/afk:fix`'

criterion: caller whose contract the diff changed but did not update
finding: Fix hands diagnose its own linked worktree, where diagnose leaves DIAGNOSIS.md and the failing test uncommitted; nothing says what the caller's commit does with them.
why: The caller set changed from 'separate diagnosis worktree' to 'uncommitted files in the caller's worktree' with no instruction to include or exclude them.
fix: State in fix what happens to the uncommitted DIAGNOSIS.md and failing test in a handed worktree.
evidence: diagnose Phase 7 step 4: 'In a handed-over worktree, leave both uncommitted for the invoker.'; FIXER-PROMPT.md:31 'commit on {FIX_BRANCH}, push'

criterion: caller routing of fix's new outcome
finding: Fix reports `blocked` for V-2/V-3 without a still-small row and for V-4; D-16(b) defers caller routing to slice 0009.
why: Callers still expect fix to fix.
fix: Confirm slice 0009 names execute and preflight as its own consumers; otherwise add an IOU.

finding: Re-run detection derives the branch from `git.branch-template` and the work id, which prose cannot do for a template with {user} or other placeholders, and a stale same-name branch silently becomes the Diagnosis branch.
why: A re-run is missed or unrelated work is reused.
fix: Detect a re-run by the owner record (which names the branch) and leave branch derivation to create-worktree.
evidence: diagnose:34 'or the local branch `git.branch-template` makes from the work id, makes this a re-run'; scripts/create-worktree:244-257

finding: D-14 'Supersedes' quotes D-11 text that does not appear in D-11; the quoted sentence is from the old diagnose step 5.
why: An entry supersedes exactly the passage it quotes, so D-11's real wording stays un-superseded.
evidence: Supersedes: D-11 "an invoker may hand over a linked worktree already cut for this bug from the Base tip in owned mode"

finding: grill-solution says the no-PRD grill 'ends at that call whatever it is', but SIZE-CALL.md now stops with no size call for a verdict other than V-2/V-3.
why: Two homes give a different end for a V-1, V-4 or V-5 diagnosis.
fix: Point the end condition at SIZE-CALL.md, covering the no-open-question stop.
evidence: SIZE-CALL.md:10 'Any other verdict leaves no open question: name it and stop with no size call.' vs grill-solution:14
